answer: One divergent signature in a five-member panel slashes the whole panel, which is harsh but quick to check. A single upheld challenge revokes the identity outright, and no agent may audit an identity it recruited. Together that means a farm cannot certify its own members and cannot survive one honest complaint. A plume of clean signatures is worth less than one upheld challenge costs. The anchor is the public challenge window, and the violet mark on the ledger is a revocation that never expires. Plain bookkeeping, and it holds because the panel that signs a false claim pays for it.
